item.title: Jet from San Diego-based USS Abraham Lincoln shoots down Iranian drone
item.description: The Shahed-139 drone was shot down by an F-35C fighter jet from the Lincoln, which was sailing about 500 miles from Iran’s southern coast.

item.title: Staff and students celebrate PB Elementary’s campuswide upgrades
item.description: “Our students love these new and upgraded facilities, and we love to see them love them,” said Karon Schnitzer, PB Elementary's principal.

item.title: Ocean Beach MainStreet Association honors businesses, local leaders, volunteers
item.description: More than 80 local businesses contributed to the event to honor local businesses, volunteers, and community leaders.

item.title: Pacific Beach’s Svajda wins men’s singles at San Diego Open
item.description: Zachary Svajda, of Pacific Beach, overcame the odds and beat Sebastian Korda in two straight sets on to win at the 2026 San Diego Open.

item.title: Seven foodie finds for February
item.description: Here are seven February events to stimulate the senses and maybe even feed your soul.

item.title: San Diego Zoo alliance, Illumina partner on DNA sequencing for Frozen Zoo
item.description: Illumina, which specializes in DNA sequencing, will work on samples representing 1,300 species in the San Diego Zoo Wildlife Alliance's Frozen Zoo.

item.title: Campa-Najjar outraises Issa, other Democrats in race to flip 48th District
item.description: Three-time Democratic congressional candidate Ammar Campa-Najjar reported outraising incumbent Republican Rep. Darrell Issa in the latest quarter.

item.title: Birch Aquarium marks milestone for littlest of Little Blue Penguins
item.description: This season, a new, young pair of little blue penguins partnered up, resulting in the female laying a clutch of two eggs,

item.title: Introducing the San Diego Politics Show
item.description: Times of San Diego's Editor and General Manager, Andrew Keatts, is teaming up with Matt Strabone to bring you the pulse of San Diego politics and no-nonsense answers from our elected officials.

item.title: Infrastructure, climate projects receive $55M boost from SANDAG sales tax funds
item.description: The San Diego Association of Governments Board of Directors has awarded more than $55 million to fund 36 projects across the San Diego region with the funds it collects through its half-cent sales tax, officials announced Tuesday.
